raw_text:
Great—thanks for the context. Below is a structured 12-week postpartum return-to-exercise plan for a 33-year-old client who is four weeks post uncomplicated cesarean, cleared for light activity with restrictions (no abs, no heavy lifting until six-week check) and training at home with only a yoga mat. The plan progresses gradually from gentle activation and mobility to more structured conditioning, with a strong emphasis on core safety, pelvic floor engagement, diastasis awareness (if applicable), posture, and overall conditioning. Always confirm with her medical team if there are evolving restrictions or symptoms (pain, heavy bleeding, or abdominal separation).

Program philosophy
- Focus on safe reintroduction of movement, diaphragmatic breathing, pelvic floor and transversus abdominis (TA) engagement, hip stability, and gradual loading.
- No traditional sit-ups, crunches, planks if diastasis is present or if instructed; progress to anti-extension and core control patterns as appropriate.
- Emphasize maternal feel-good training, sleep hygiene, nutrition, hydration, and recovery.
- Week 4 activity is light; weeks 5–12 progress gradually with attention to core rehab and gradual conditioning.

Structure
- Frequency: 3 days/week resistance + 2–3 optional light mobility/conditioning days, 5–6 days of light activity (walking) as tolerated.
- Equipment: yoga mat only (no weights). We will progress from bodyweight to gentler resistance with tempo and time under tension, and introduce light isometrics and scapular work.
- Core approach: diaphragmatic breathing, pelvic floor recruitment, TA activation, pelvic mobility, and gradual reintroduction of low-load, low-impact core work (no traditional loaded abdominal exercises). If diastasis recti is present and visibly separates >2 cm or with a clinician’s guidance, avoid high-load core exercises and progress per medical advice.

Important guidelines
- Stop immediately if: vaginal bleeding increases, pain in the lower back or pelvis worsens, or any new symptoms like pressure, dizziness, or lightheadedness.
- Warm-up with 5–8 minutes of gentle mobilization and diaphragmatic breathing before every session.
- Keep intensity low to moderate; RPE should be 3–5/10 initially, gradually rising to 5–6/10 by Week 12 for conditioning components.
- Include daily pelvic floor checks: inhale to relax, exhale and gently engage pelvic floor (as if stopping urine flow). Maintain that engagement during exercises where appropriate.

Week-by-week plan

Phase 1: Reconnect and protect (Weeks 1–2)
Goals: Establish diaphragmatic breathing, pelvic floor activation, hip mobility, and basic movement patterns with minimal spinal load.

Weeks 1–2 (3x per week)
Session A (Lower Body & Pelvic Floor)
- 5–8 minute warm-up: diaphragmatic breathing (core engage on exhale), hip circles, gentle leg pumps (supine, 10–12 each side).
- Pelvic floor activation: 2 sets x 6–8 reps of gentle floor contraction with inhale-expire cycle; hold 2–3 seconds, relax 3 seconds.
- Glute bridges (modified): 2 sets x 8–10 reps (hips lift with control; avoid spine extension strain). If comfortable, progress to marching bridge: 2 sets x 6–8 each leg.
- Side-lying clams: 2 sets x 10–12 per side (sleeved to ensure knee alignment; keep spine neutral).
- Wall-assisted hip flexor release: 2 sets x 30 seconds per side (gentle stretch without pain).
- Cool-down: diaphragmatic breathing 2–3 minutes; gentle hamstring and quadriceps light stretch.

Session B (Upper Body & Posture)
- 5–8 minute warm-up: shoulder circles, scapular retractions, wall thoracic mobility (hands on wall at shoulder height, rotate).
- Isometric scapular set: 2–3 sets x 6–8 reps (squeeze shoulder blades together while maintaining neutral spine).
- Push-up progression: incline push-up against wall or countertop, 2 sets x 6–8 reps; ensure ribcage remains stable; avoid funneling belly.
- Seated band (or towel) row substitute: if no bands, perform “reverse fly” with light isometrics: 2 sets x 8 reps, hold 2 seconds at peak.
- Plank alternative safety check: avoid traditional planks; instead perform dead bug progression (supine) with pelvic floor engagement: 2–3 sets x 6–8 reps per side (opposite arm/leg extension without spine flexion).
- Cool-down: chest and upper back stretch, gentle neck release.

Session C (Mobility & Light Conditioning)
- 5–8 minute warm-up: diaphragmatic breathing, gentle spinal mobility (cat-cow limited, no deep flexion).
- Pelvic tilts on all fours (if comfortable, otherwise supine): 2–3 sets x 10 reps with breath control.
- Pelvic floor-friendly dead bug variations: 2 sets x 8 reps per side, slow tempo.
- Bird dog (modified): 2 sets x 6 reps per side, focus on keeping pelvis stable and ribcage centered.
- Glute activation: glute bridges or hip thrust hold at top for 2–3 seconds, 2 sets x 8.
- Cool-down: hip flexor/groin stretch, lower back gentle stretch.

Phase 2: Base conditioning and core progression (Weeks 3–4)
Goals: Build foundational strength, maintain pelvic floor engagement, introduce light core-safe loading, and reintroduce gentle cardio.

Weeks 3–4 (3x per week; 1–2 optional mobility days)
Session A (Lower Body & Core Safety)
- 5–8 minute warm-up: breathing drill (diaphragm), hip circles.
- Glute bridge progression: 2–3 sets x 10–12 reps; add a pause at the top for 1–2 seconds.
- Split stance hip hinge (floor-based): 2–3 sets x 8 reps per leg (posterior chain focus; keep torso angle controlled).
- Side-lying hydrant with external rotation: 2 sets x 10–12 per side to enhance hip stability.
- TA activation circuit: supine or hook-lying, 2–3 sets x 10–12 slow breaths with pelvic floor lift on exhale.
- Gentle cardio: 10–15 minutes of brisk walking or step-ups on a sturdy platform if available.

Session B (Upper Body + Core Stability)
- 5–8 minute warm-up: scapula mobilization, thoracic extension on wall.
- Push-up variation: incline or wall push-ups, 2–3 sets x 8–10 reps.
- Seated rows (towel or light resistance): 2–3 sets x 10–12 reps (focus on scapular retraction, no rib flare).
- Anti-extension cueing: quadruped vs. tall kneeling with a light thoracic brace (no spine hyperextension) for 2–3 sets x 8–10 seconds holds.
- Dead bug progression: 2–3 sets x 8–10 reps per side with controlled breathing.
- Core-friendly hip stability drill: standing hip abduction with light resistance from a loop if available; otherwise bodyweight 2 sets x 12 per side.

Session C (Mobility, Conditioning, and Core Work)
- 5–8 minute warm-up: dynamic hip openers.
- Lying leg raise progressions: supine with knee bent, 2–3 sets x 8–10 reps if diastasis not active; otherwise skip.
- Glute bridge with march: 2–3 sets x 8–10 reps per leg.
- Standing marches with pelvic floor engagement: 2–3 sets x 20 seconds.
- Gentle cardio finisher: 5–10 minutes of brisk walking or stationary march in place.

Week 5–6: Reintroduce light loaded movement and more conditioning (Phase 3)
Goals: Start controlled resistance-like loading through tempo and isometrics, increase overall work capacity, continue protecting core.

Weeks 5–6 (3–4x per week; 1 optional mobility day)
Session A (Lower Body)
- 5–8 minute warm-up with breath work.
- Hip hinge with short range deadlift pattern (no external load): 3 sets x 8–10 reps, tempo 3-1-2 (eccentric slow).
- Glute bridge with single-leg option (non-loaded if needed): 3 sets x 8–10 per leg.
- Clamshells with resistance (if available, light) or without: 3 sets x 12 per side.
- Standing hip abduction with light isometric hold at top: 2–3 sets x 12 reps per leg.
- Core: dead bug with leg extension alternative, 2–3 sets x 8–10 reps per side.

Session B (Upper Body)
- 5–8 minute warm-up.
- Incline push-ups or knee push-ups: 3 sets x 8–10 reps.
- Seated row with light towel or resistance: 3 sets x 10–12 reps.
- Shoulder isometrics: 2–3 sets x 10–15 seconds holds.
- Pallof press substitute (standing with resistance, if available) or anti-rotation cueing: 2–3 sets x 8–10 seconds holds per side.
- Mobility: thoracic spine reach and lat stretch.

Session C (Conditioning & Core)
- 5–8 minute warm-up.
- Marching or step-ups (low height) 2–3 sets x 12–15 reps per leg.
- Glute bridge hold 2–3 sets x 15–20 seconds at top.
- Bird dog with extended hold: 2–3 sets x 8–10 reps per side.
- TA activation circuit: 3 sets x 12 slow breaths with pelvic floor lift.
- Light cardio finisher: 10–15 minutes of brisk walk or easy cycling if available.

Optional Session D (Mobility/Recovery)
- 20–30 minutes of yoga-based mobility focusing on hips, spine, and diaphragmatic breathing.

Phase 4: Build strength and conditioning (Weeks 7–9)
Goals: Increase movement complexity with safe core integration, begin gentle total-body conditioning, improve endurance.

Weeks 7–9 (3–4x per week)
Session A (Lower Body Strength & Core)
- 8 minute warm-up: dynamic mobility, breath-based activation.
- Hip hinge with tempo: 3 sets x 10–12 reps, tempo 3-1-2.
- Glute bridge with hold: 3 sets x 12–15 seconds hold at top; 2–3 reps for quality.
- Split squat (bodyweight): 3 sets x 8–10 per leg; ensure knee tracks over toes.
- Side-lying clam with hold at top for 2 seconds: 3 sets x 12 per side.
- Core: quadruped opposite arm/leg raise (bird dog) with slower tempo: 3 sets x 8 reps per side.

Session B (Upper Body & Core)
- 8 minute warm-up: scapular stability, thoracic mobility.
- Push-ups progressions: incline to floor as able (if core tolerated), 3 sets x 6–10 reps.
- Row variations: seated or standing with towel or bands; 3 sets x 12 reps.
- Scapular push-ups: 2–3 sets x 10–12 reps.
- Anti-rotation holds (Pallof or column tap): 3 sets x 8–10 seconds per side.

Session C (Full Body Conditioning)
- 8–10 minute warm-up.
- Hip/shoulder complex: thoracic reach, hip twist with support, 3 rounds.
- Bodyweight circuit: 3 rounds (8–12 reps each, minimal rest)
  - Squat to chair (sit-to-stand) or half-squat with tempo
  - Push-ups or incline push-ups
  - Glute bridge or hip thrust hold
  - Bird dog or dead bug
- Cardio finisher: 12–18 minutes steady brisk walk or step-up intervals (2 minutes work, 1 minute rest)

Weeks 10–12: Strength and conditioning consolidation (Phase 5)
Goals: Solidify gains, increase conditioning density, maintain core safety, and reintroduce more varied movement patterns.

Weeks 10–12 (3–4x per week)
Session A (Lower Body Strength)
- Warm-up with dynamic mobility.
- Goblet-like movement without weight: isometric holds at depth and tempo squats using chair as a target, 3 sets x 10–12 reps with controlled tempo (0.5–1 second descent, 1–2 second pause at bottom if comfortable).
- Romanian hinge with light loading substitute: 3 sets x 8–10 reps, but no actual weight; focus on hip hinge.
- Step-ups to box (low height): 3 sets x 8–10 per leg.
- Core: dead bug with alternating arm/leg 2–3 sets x 8–12 reps per side.

Session B (Upper Body Strength & Core Stability)
- Warm-up: thoracic mobility and scapular work.
- Push-ups: 3–4 sets x 8–12 reps (progress toward floor if ready).
- Inverted row on low bar or towel row (if feasible, else continue with incline push-ups): 3–4 sets x 10–12 reps.
- Rotational anti-core work: standing anti-rotation press using towel or resistance (or lifelike hold) 3 sets x 8–10 seconds per side.
- Core: side plank progression if diastasis not a concern or with clinician guidance; otherwise continue safe core patterns.

Session C (Conditioning & Return-to-Run Prep, if desired)
- 5–8 minute warm-up.
- Conditioning circuit: 4 rounds of 40 seconds work / 20 seconds rest
  - Bodyweight squat to rise
  - Hip hinge walk
  - Step-up march
  - Scapular push-ups
- Optional walk/jog intervals to begin assessing tolerance: 2–3 minutes jog, 2 minutes walk, repeat 2–3 times if tolerated.

Nutritional and recovery guidance
- Hydration: aim for 2.5–3.5 liters per day, adjusting for climate and breastfeeding status.
- Protein: target 1.2–1.6 g/kg/day to support tissue repair and recovery. Include lean protein with each meal.
- Carbohydrates: align with energy needs, particularly for breastfeeding; prioritize complex carbohydrates, fruits, vegetables, and whole grains.
- Fat intake: include healthy fats (omega-3s from fish, flaxseed, chia, nuts) to support mood and energy.
- Sleep: prioritize sleep when possible; short naps of 20–40 minutes can help recovery.
- Postpartum considerations: monitor for signs of diastasis recti and pelvic floor issues; consult a pelvic floor physical therapist if there are concerns about heavy leakage, continued separation, or pain.

Return-to-run guidance
- If the client desires, start run-walk intervals after Week 8 only if core control and pelvic floor are stable and no symptoms arise.
- Start with 1–2 minutes running with 2–3 minutes walking, gradually increasing running time week by week while listening to body.

Progression notes
- If any exercise increases separation or pain, regress to previous week’s safer patterns and consider pelvic floor physical therapy or clinician guidance.
- Emphasize quality over quantity; keep sessions focused on form, breathing, and pelvic stability.
- Use tempo and time-under-tension to create loading without added weight.
